title: The Value of Silence: The Effect of UMG's Licensing Dispute with TikTok on Music Demand
authors: Mengjie Cheng; Elie Ofek; Hema Yoganarasimhan
eligible_reason: Single adoption date. The treatment is UMG-label track x post (the UMG-TikTok licensing dispute began on one date, February 1, 2024, for all UMG tracks); `post` is a common calendar indicator and sound_track_labels_universal_val is time-invariant. Every regression is reghdfe y 1.sound_track_labels_universal_val#1.post, absorb(sound_track_uid date_dt) (Tables 3, 7, 8, 9, 10). One treated cohort, so the at-least-two-adoption-dates rule fails.
design_notes: Track-day panel (Soundcharts/Chartmetric): daily Spotify streams and YouTube views for UMG (treated) vs. Warner/Sony (control) tracks around the Feb 2024 UMG-TikTok dispute. Table 3: log outcomes, full sample (VoS_code.do lines 94-95). Table 7: split by on_tiktok_pre (lines 141-148). Table 8: tracks not on TikTok pre-dispute split by artist TikTok coverage (lines 155-161). Table 9: levels (168-169). Table 10: levels dropping >p99 (178-182). Track FE + date FE, cluster by track, no controls.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One event date (Feb 1, 2024) for all UMG tracks.

specs.notes: YouTube views analogue at line 95; Tables 7-10 are subsamples/levels of the same spec.

data_files: replication_data_code/datasample.dta (random 10% of tracks from the proprietary full dataset; README says estimates differ from the paper)
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Design read from VoS_code.do; `post` has no track-specific variation in the data dictionary ('whether it's after the dispute').
